paper_metadata.title: High-temperature strength of nickel alloys based on γ'-phase

evidence.quote: Ternary and quaternary alloys have been studied, based on the Ni-Al-Ta and Ni-Al-Hf systems, with aluminium contents in the range 10-25 at.-%, tantalum or hafnium contents up to 5 at.-%, and carbon up to 1.4 at.-%.

The yield strengths of the alloys derive predominantly from solid-solution strengthening.
This is attributable to carbide formation causing solute depletion of the matrix, particularly in tantalum and hafnium, and hence reducing the solid-solution strengthening
Tantalum and hafnium produce substantial solid-solution strengthening in aluminium-rich γ'.
the hardness and room-temperature strength were lower than for the corresponding ternary alloys (7C and 10C). This is attributable to carbide formation causing solute depletion of the matrix
Alloy 5 exhibits an increase in creep resistance after homogenizing at 1320°C and aging at 1000°C, analogous with the increase in yield stress.
